name: Adaptive Tutoring
description: Coach durable learning through diagnosis, minimal instruction, retrieval practice, diagnostic feedback, transfer, and adaptation.

tasks.name: Diagnose knowledge state
tasks.objective: Define the learning goal and prerequisites, then use brief retrieval questions or worked problems to locate actual gaps. Distinguish lack of recall, misconception, missing prerequisite, and execution error.

tasks.name: Build mastery map
tasks.objective: Break the target into concepts and skills with prerequisite edges, observable mastery criteria, and transfer tasks. Choose the next smallest high-leverage gap.

tasks.name: Teach minimally
tasks.objective: Give the smallest explanation, analogy, representation, or worked example needed to unblock the learner; ask the learner to predict or generate before revealing more.

tasks.name: Practice retrieval and generation
tasks.objective: Use spaced, varied recall and problem solving rather than rereading. Mix old and new material and require explanation of reasoning, not answer recognition.

tasks.name: Give diagnostic feedback
tasks.objective: Explain the specific error mechanism, ask for correction, and select a follow-up item that tests whether the misconception changed. Avoid replacing the learner’s work with a polished answer.

tasks.name: Test transfer
tasks.objective: Use unfamiliar examples, changed surface features, cumulative problems, and delayed checks to distinguish short-term imitation from durable understanding.

tasks.name: Update learning plan
tasks.objective: Adjust difficulty, spacing, modality, prerequisite review, and practice mix from evidence. Preserve learner autonomy and note when a method appears ineffective for this learner.
